name: Walkaloosa
notes: A gaited Appaloosa: the Walkaloosa Horse Registry, founded 1983, registers horses that have both verified Appaloosa ancestry and a certified intermediate gait that is not a trot. The early crosses were largely Appaloosa on Paso Fino. Two inherited things at once is the whole breed.

LP is fixed in the regular strain - every fully registered founder carries at least one copy, because visible Appaloosa colour from ten feet away is a registration requirement rather than a preference. PATN1 and PATN2 sit high behind it so blankets, snowcaps, leopards and few-spots are the common outcomes rather than varnish alone.

Two strains, 9 regular to 1 identification-only. The registry issues ID papers to horses that lack the colour or the gait, and that is what the second strain is; it carries LP at a trace instead of not at all.

It is leopard and not pinto, and the file is built to keep that true: tobiano, frame, sabino, splash and the W-series are all forced wild. A nearly white few-spot Walkaloosa is still an Appaloosa-patterned horse.

Grey is forced wild on the registry's own logic - it would progressively obscure the pattern the horse is registered for. Mushroom, silver, champagne and pearl are out too; cream, dun, roan and flaxen stay in at low rates as legitimate bases under the pattern.
DMRT3 sits high for the gait requirement. The running walk, fox trot, rack, single-foot and stepping pace are not modelled, nor is the gait certification.

All disorders clear. The one real health consequence is LP/LP congenital stationary night blindness, and it belongs to the leopard locus rather than to the disorder panel - the mod already reports it there, informationally, and it costs the horse nothing.
